display.purpose: Page titles and the score at display size (34px, Archivo 700).

meta.purpose: Mono values and meta (15px, IBM Plex Mono, tabular).

label.purpose: Column heads, units, status tags, group labels (13px mono, 0.06em, often uppercase).

shadows.name: elev-light-only
shadows.purpose: The single permitted elevation, light theme only, where a panel must lift off paper. Never on dark.

motion.name: press
motion.purpose: Global active-press feedback on every enabled button.

motion.name: focus-ring
motion.purpose: Focus-visible ring on buttons and inputs; never animate its appearance.

breakpoints.name: md
breakpoints.purpose: First-run two-column collapses to one column below this.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The one amber action per screen.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; height: 32px; padding: 0 12px; background: #e8a33d; color: #0b0b0c; border: none; border-radius: 9999px; font-family: Archivo, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 500; cursor: pointer; transition: background .2s, transform .1s, filter .1s; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: #eab258; } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px rgba(232,163,61,0.5); } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform: translateY(1px); filter: brightness(0.9); }

components.name: Ghost Button
components.description: A non-primary action; carries most of the interface so amber stays rare.
components.css: .ds-btn-ghost { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; height: 32px; padding: 0 12px; background: transparent; color: #f2f2f0; border: none; border-radius: 9999px; font-family: Archivo, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 500; cursor: pointer; transition: background .2s; } .ds-btn-ghost:hover { background: #1c1c1f; } .ds-btn-ghost:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px rgba(232,163,61,0.5); }

components.name: Surface Card
components.description: A raised panel, square, separated by tone and a hairline — no shadow on dark.
components.html:

components.css: .ds-card { background: #141416; border: 1px solid #1f1f23; border-radius: 0; padding: 16px; } .ds-card-label { font-family: 'IBM Plex Mono', monospace; font-size: 13px; letter-spacing: 0.06em; text-transform: uppercase; color: #868682; } .ds-card-title { margin: 12px 0 0; font-family: Archivo, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 24px; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: -0.01em; color: #f2f2f0; }

components.name: Input Field
components.description: Square field on ground, amber focus language shared with buttons.
components.css: .ds-input { width: 100%; background: #0b0b0c; color: #f2f2f0; border: 1px solid #3e3e46; border-radius: 0; padding: 8px 10px; font-family: 'IBM Plex Mono', monospace; font-size: 15px; } .ds-input::placeholder { color: #55554f; } .ds-input:focus-visible { outline: none; border-color: #e8a33d; box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px rgba(232,163,61,0.5); }

components.name: Status Tag
components.description: A mono status label — verdict green for a passing state, faint for a locked one.
components.css: .ds-tag { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; font-family: 'IBM Plex Mono', monospace; font-size: 13px; letter-spacing: 0.06em; color: #6fad86; }

narrative.overview: Crowsnest looks like a precise measuring tool, not a marketing surface. The screen is a panel of readouts: neutral by default, dense with real numbers, and lit by a single amber signal that means one thing only — this post beat its channel's own median. Everything that is not that signal recedes to a graded neutral scale. The system runs dark by default and swaps to a warm-paper light theme; both keep the same discipline. Display and body are Archivo; every number, unit, label, and status tag is IBM Plex Mono with tabular figures. Corners are square on every surface, and the only rounded thing in the product is the button, a pill that reads as the one place you act. Depth is nearly absent: dark is flat and separates planes by tone, and only light is allowed a single soft elevation.
keyCharacteristics: Amber is a signal, not a brand color — reserved for the score and one action per screen.
Every number is monospaced and tabular; uppercase appears only on column heads and group labels.
Square corners on all surfaces; pill only on buttons.
Flat by default; depth is tonal, not shadowed (light theme excepted).
Dark-first, with a warm-paper light theme carrying the same rules.

rules.name: The Amber Law
rules.body: Amber means exactly one thing: this beat its channel's median. It is allowed on the score and on one primary action per screen. It is banned on nav-active state, toggles, secondary buttons, the logo, progress bars, and count badges, which use a raised neutral surface instead.

rules.name: The Two-Hue Rule
rules.body: The only chromatic colors are amber (signal) and red (failure), with green as the muted positive verdict. Series are told apart with neutral inks, never invented hues.

rules.name: The Tabular Number Rule
rules.body: Every number is monospace and tabular-nums slashed-zero. Aligned digits are what make the product read as a tool.

rules.name: The Uppercase Budget
rules.body: Uppercase appears only on column heads and group labels, at 0.06em. Never uppercase a heading, a button, or body copy.

rules.name: The Flat Console Rule
rules.body: Depth is tonal, not cast. Reach for a lighter surface and a hairline before a shadow; on dark, never reach for a shadow at all.

dos: Do keep amber for the score and one primary action per screen; carry everything else on neutral surfaces.
Do set every number in IBM Plex Mono with tabular, slashed-zero figures.
Do keep surfaces square (0px) and let the pill button be the only rounded form.
Do separate planes with tone and a hairline; on dark, use no shadow.
Do reserve uppercase for column heads and group labels, at 0.06em.
donts: Don't put amber on nav-active state, toggles, secondary buttons, the logo, progress bars, or count badges.
Don't introduce a third chromatic hue, or a green loud enough to rival amber.
Don't round card, input, or panel corners, and don't wrap surfaces in shadows on the dark theme.
Don't set numbers in a proportional font or drop tabular figures.
Don't invent metrics, counts, or states the app cannot actually produce.
